design_reference: Editeur Livre-Jeu - Wireframes.dc.html § 02 side panel « NŒUD #4 »: sticky header (NodeBadge + ref + title + ✕); sections — Libellé du choix, Description, Illustration (deferred), Objets à prendre, Action requise (SegmentedControl + delegated body), Choix sortants, Fin victoire/Fin échec toggles. Anatomy + tokens from styles.css.

plan.goal: Edit a single leaf's content in a side panel beside the tree — text, inventory, the required-action block (delegated to action-* via ActionRegistry), outgoing choices (delegated to choice-linking), and the victory/failure end toggles.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a node (node:selected) opens the side panel populated with that node's content read from BookService; the header shows the node's NodeBadge + ref + title.
Editing the description updates the node via BookService and emits node:updated; edits survive reload; empty fields show inviting placeholders.

The « Action requise » SegmentedControl reflects the node's current action type; changing it emits action:changed{actionType} and swaps in the matching editor resolved from ActionRegistry — node-editor contains no action-specific logic.
Adding/removing inventory objects updates the node's « objets à prendre » via BookService/ObjectCatalogService; objects carry a name AND a player-facing description (shared ObjectEditor).
Toggling « Fin victoire » / « Fin échec » sets the node's end flags via BookService; turning a node into an end is reflected by its NodeBadge updating to the FIN mark on canvas/outline.

Sommaire and Mort are structural screens: the panel hides « libellé du choix », « action requise » and the Fin toggles for both, and hides « choix sortants » for Mort; only the text is editable (enforced in BookService.updateNode too).
The « Choix sortants » area and footer branch/relink actions are provided by choice-linking mounted in the reserved slot; node-editor does not duplicate edge logic.
The Illustration section renders as a deferred/disabled dropzone (no upload), without breaking layout.
Closing the panel (✕) deselects without losing committed edits; switching selection swaps content without leaking the previous node's field state.
The whole panel renders from design-system components/tokens, light theme; controls have ≥44px targets and the panel is keyboard-navigable.
plan.walking_skeleton: On selection, load the node from BookService and render the panel shell with the Description Field and the end toggles, committing edits via BookService.updateNode (emit node:updated). Render the Action SegmentedControl and mount the editor resolved from ActionRegistry for the current type. Reserve the libellé/illustration/inventory/choices slots as deferred placeholders. Compose canvas + panel in the app shell.

iterations.goal: Panel shell + text/toggles: faithful § 02 layout, sticky header with NodeBadge, Description Field with placeholder, Fin victoire/échec toggles wired to BookService (node:updated). DS fidelity.

Action block via ActionRegistry: SegmentedControl reflects + sets action type, emits action:changed, mounts the registered editor; zero action-specific code in node-editor (KR-051). Registry seam shipped; concrete editors arrive with action-* features.

Inventory + shared ObjectEditor: add/remove « objets à prendre » as Chips, open the shared brain ObjectEditor (name + player-facing description + effect), persist via ObjectCatalogService/BookService (KR-052).

Edit-safety + slots: debounced commits without focus loss, clean content swap (KR-053), mount choice-linking + editable libellé (on the incoming edge) in the choices slot, deferred Illustration dropzone, full a11y/keyboard pass.

known_risks: KR-050 — node-editor is a HOST shell: the action body and the choices list are mounted from other features via ActionRegistry / feature slots. Importing an action feature directly would break feature isolation.
KR-051 — Adding a new action type must require ZERO changes here: the SegmentedControl options + mounted editor come from the ActionRegistry. Hard-coding a type couples node-editor to a specialty.
KR-052 — Objects carry a player-facing DESCRIPTION, not just a name — the inventory editor must capture both via the shared ObjectEditor, never a bare string.
KR-053 — Selection swap must not leak the previous node's uncommitted field state into the next node; reset/keyed panel state on selection change.
KR-054 — Turning a node into a Fin (victory/échec) changes its kind/badge everywhere; the end flags live on the node in BookService so canvas/outline reflect it via node:updated.

KR-055 — Sommaire (root) and Mort (death leaf) are structural: no libellé, no required action, no Fin toggles; Mort also has no outgoing choices. Text-only — enforced in the panel AND in BookService.updateNode.
KR-024 — Selection is owned by the SelectionService (SSOT); node-editor reacts and may set it (deselect on ✕) but holds no competing copy.
KR-011 — No raw localStorage; all node data via BookService.
KR-013 — Field values bind to the store/handlers, not useEffect-mirrored copies of props.

iterations_log.label: walking-skeleton (+ iteration 1)
architecture_choices: Promoted selection to a brain SelectionService (single source of truth, KR-024): tree-canvas and node-editor both read via useSelectedNode and write via selection.select; the service is the sole emitter of node:selected and clears selection on book:opened. This replaced tree-canvas's local selection state and lets the panel's ✕ deselect without desyncing the canvas highlight.

node-editor is a HOST shell (KR-050): it owns the frame + Description + end toggles + the action SLOT, and mounts the action editor resolved from the brain ActionRegistry — no action-* import. SegmentedControl options derive from the registry, so adding an action type needs zero changes here (KR-051).
Fields bind directly to BookService (via updateNode) with no local mirror; the panel subtree is keyed by node id so a selection swap cannot leak stale field state (KR-053).
End flags live on the node (endVictory/endFailure); brain util effectiveKind/endLabel derives the FIN badge so canvas + panel reflect it from one source via node:updated (KR-054).
BookService.updateNode enforces the lock rule (KR-002): a locked node accepts only text edits. Shared view logic (useOpenBook, nodeTitle) promoted to brain so both features reuse it (KR-110).
App shell composes tree-canvas + node-editor side-by-side (§ 02); the two features never import each other — they talk only through brain (selection + BookService).
deviations_from_plan: Libellé du choix is DEFERRED: it lives on the incoming edge (user decision), so its editable field arrives with choice-linking. The skeleton showed a read-only note in the libellé slot pointing authors to the parent's « Choix sortants »; once choice-linking shipped the editable label there (iter 1), the note was clutter on every node and was REMOVED (user request) — the panel no longer renders a libellé section.
Inventory (iter 3) and the choices slot mount (iter 4) render as deferred placeholders; Illustration upload stays disabled (no image scope).

Iteration 2's ActionRegistry SEAM is shipped in the skeleton (SegmentedControl + registry mount + action:changed), but concrete action editors land with the action-* features, so iter 2 stays planned.

test_coverage.unit: SelectionService (select/emit/idempotent/cross-book clear); BookService.updateNode (text+flags persist+emit, locked text-only guard, unknown null)
test_coverage.integration: NodeEditorPanel: empty-state, select+edit Description via BookService, Fin victoire toggle flips FIN badge, action:changed + actionType persisted from SegmentedControl, ✕ closes + locked Mort toggles disabled

resolved_decisions: Editing happens in a persistent SIDE PANEL beside the tree.
Libellé du choix lives on the INCOMING EDGE (not duplicated on the node); edited via choice-linking.
Selection is a brain SelectionService consumed by both canvas and panel (SSOT).
Illustration deferred (disabled placeholder); inventory + choices are mounted/expanded in later iterations.
node-editor owns text/toggles; action bodies and choices come from other features via ActionRegistry / slots.
Sommaire and Mort are structural screens (KR-055): no libellé / action / Fin toggles; Mort also has no outgoing choices; text-only, enforced at the SSOT.
open_questions: ObjectCatalogService shape (iteration 3) — define when action-decor's object model lands.
Debounce strategy for Description commits (iteration 4) vs the current commit-on-change.
